figures.name: Cost watcher on the first real cost refresh (31 Oct 2026, both KS layers)
figures.label: measured
figures.method: The replica's costs refreshed that morning; the feed read the costs of the SKUs no other rule owns that sit near their floor, and 293 had moved at least 0.5 % from the engine run's. No rise was raised: 102 of the 156 rises left the live price above its floor, 52 put it under but the price was a cheaper deal (held for a person: the publisher leaves those alone), and 2 had a floor above max(anchor, current) (held: the regular price needs changing); no jump looked like a data error. The rebuild spanned two polls: 168 of the 461 observations were the same moves seen again (each held a second time); the feed now skips a cost already observed since the run. What held the 52 (Prompt 10, on the sandbox's discounts at the observation): 28 the calculator's own earlier push (an October set the team imported, carrying a price an approval gave that SKU), 21 only an app-only deal (no longer a hold: the web price is ours, written since 31 Oct), 3 a real team deal. With the go-live switch on (own pushes superseded), 49 of the 52 would have been raised; with it off (the default), 21. Ten observations were checked by hand against the engine run (hours.md, 31 Oct).
figures.source: ai.CostObservation, ai.AgentDecision, ai.PublishException, the sandbox discounts, PricingTool.Approvals / ApprovalItems
